title: Hiring a cashier
summary: Once the shop is busy you stop being the only person at the till: Supermarket Simulator defines a cashier as its own thing, with a hiring data object and cashier-specific items.
body: A cashier is a defined kind of worker in the game rather than a generic helper, so hiring is a distinct decision from buying equipment.
Cashier behaviour has its own animation handling, which is why the till looks different when staffed.
The checkout itself is what the cashier uses, and that checkout logic is separate from the hiring decision.
What this entry does not tell you: wages, hiring costs, how many cashiers you can have or how fast they scan. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: A cashier is a defined worker type in the game.
Cashier-specific items exist, separate from the checkout machine.
The checkout a cashier uses is separate logic from hiring.
The build names a cashier avatar and a control transform of its own for the person behind the till.
The cashier comes with her own avatar entry and two further levels of detail.
The staff are shipped as named models: several restockers, a woman cashier and counter helpers, a bakery helper and an ice cream helper among them.
facts.evidence: asset names: Restocker_02, Restocker_06, Restocker_Female, Woman_Cashier, Bakery_Helper, Ice_Cream_Helper
